label: Heeren 1817 restricts exact colour-based classification because chromatic variation is too nuanced and insufficiently known
subject: agent.arnold-hermann-ludwig-heeren
object: bodily colour as basis for classifying peoples/types

sources.citation: Heinrich von Gagern, Kollegnachschrift of Heeren's Allgemeine Länder- und Völkerkunde, summer semester 1817; excerpts edited in Christoph Becker-Schaum, Arnold Herrmann Ludwig Heeren (Frankfurt a.M.: Peter Lang, 1993), pp. 307-319, relevant p. 311
André de Melo Araújo, Weltgeschichte in Göttingen (Bielefeld: transcript, 2012), p. 209

observations.value: An exact classification of all peoples/types cannot be made because there are too many colour nuances and they are insufficiently known; only coarse Hauptvölker characterised by dominant colours can be classified.
The problem arises before stronger historical inference: continuous or poorly measured chromatic variation must first be discretised into stable finite categories.

claim_limit: This is not direct Heeren autograph/print control. Preserve the derivative chain from lecture to Gagern transcript to Becker-Schaum edition to Araújo. Do not treat coarse Hauptvölker as a precise natural taxonomy.

label: Heeren allows historical experience to raise probability of a colour/body relation while withholding causal proof
subject: agent.arnold-hermann-ludwig-heeren
object: relation between bodily organisation associated with skin-colour differences and development of mental capacities

sources.citation: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren, Historische Werke, vol. 15 = Ideen über die Politik, den Verkehr und den Handel der vornehmsten Völker der alten Welt, part III, Europäische Völker, first division, Griechen, 4th revised ed. (Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht, 1826), pp. 5-7

observations.value: Araújo quotes Heeren asking who can prove the proposed influence between bodily organisation associated with skin-colour difference and faster/slower development of mental capacities.
Historical experience is presented as capable of increasing probability rather than proving the mechanism.
The historical pattern is not to prove absolute incapacity and is not to be treated as the sole cause.

claim_limit: 1826 is the controlled witness date, not necessarily the composition date of the passage. An edition of the Griechen division exists from 1812; compare 1812/1817/1826 openings before assigning an earlier date to the wording. Handle the historical racial claims as objects of historical analysis, not as valid modern biological propositions.

label: Meiners promotes bodily colour into a stronger causal and essential explanatory architecture
subject: agent.christoph-meiners

sources.citation: Araújo 2012, discussion of Meiners's Grundriß der Geschichte der Menschheit, 1785 and 1793 editions, pp. 168-178

observations.value: Araújo reports that the 1785 edition makes climate the main cause of bodily colour, whereas the 1793 edition promotes parental blood/descent ahead of climate.
Araújo contrasts Gatterer's refusal to make accidental Hautfarbe an organising principle with Meiners's treatment of the same feature as causa essentialis within human difference.
The case supplies a contrast in inferential entitlement: a visible category is promoted into inherited, essential and wider explanatory claims.

claim_limit: Directly control the relevant 1785 and 1793 pages before exact primary quotation. Encode this as historically situated racial anthropology and do not present the claims as valid modern science.

label: Göttingen colour cases form a comparative matrix of discretisation, classification and inference jurisdiction

observations.value: Visible bodily colour is descriptively usable but non-essential; language later outranks colour for origin inference, with colour retained under data scarcity.
Colour is promoted into stronger essential/inherited causal explanation.
Exact colour taxonomy is restricted by too many poorly known nuances; coarse categories only.
Historical recurrence can raise causal probability without supplying proof, absolute incapacity or sole-cause warrant.
The same visible domain can fail or succeed at distinct thresholds: observation, discretisation, classification, genealogy, essence and cause.

claim_limit: This is currently a comparative matrix, not proof of one explicit Göttingen colour controversy or a direct lineage of colour method among the actors. Promote only if correspondence, teaching relations or explicit cross-reference connects the cases.

label: Heraldic and bodily colour expose different discretisation regimes

observations.value: Heraldic tinctures operate in a finite conventional category-space that can be named, hatched and decoded reproducibly.
Heeren's derivative 1817 control treats bodily colour as containing too many insufficiently known nuances for exact exhaustive classification.
colour classification requires a prior discretisation regime; conventional finite colour domains and continuous poorly standardised colour domains create different epistemic possibilities.

claim_limit: This is a cross-domain analytical control, not evidence of historical transfer from heraldry to anthropology.

label: Heeren colour jurisdiction: close derivative and edition history
notes: Two Heeren colour controls now require different closure procedures: the 1817 lecture claim survives through a student transcript; the causal claim is quoted from the 1826 fourth-edition Griechen volume, with an earlier 1812 edition of that division independently attested.
reopen_rule: (1) Inspect Becker-Schaum 1993 p.311 and provenance of the Gagern 1817 transcript; if accessible, inspect the Bundesarchiv manuscript. (2) Inspect Heeren Historische Werke vol.15 (1826) pp.5-7 directly. (3) Compare corresponding opening pages in the 1812 and 1817 Griechen editions to determine first appearance of the causal wording. Do not label the passage 1793 without edition evidence.
